raw_case_text:
A 65-year-old male with history of non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (HbA1c of 6.5%) and schizoaffective disorder presented with multiple new skin lesions starting in July 2016. The patient had underlying eczema and he complained that his lesions were worsening over the prior three weeks, starting on his right knee, with subsequent spread to his left knee and bilateral upper extremities. The lesions appeared different from his baseline eczema and did not itch. The patient's primary care physician noticed this rash on the entire circumference of his upper extremities and extensor surface of his thighs bilaterally (Figure 1). The lesions were described as purple or dark red plaques and papules with a discrete circular pattern, without underlying erythema. In addition, some of the papules had minimal pustular drainage. There were fewer lesions in sun exposed areas; the patient was started on triamcinolone cream for presumed guttate psoriasis. However, he showed no improvement at follow-up three weeks later.
The patient reported no sick contacts or international travel. The only travel he reported was to Montana in April of 2016 and New Mexico in 2015, but he did not have any acute illnesses while traveling or subsequently. The patient lives with his significant other and does not have any pets at home. He denied any known insect bites.
The differential diagnosis included atypical erythema migrans, viral exanthem, tinea, or potentially Majocchi's granuloma (MG). A punch biopsy of the left medial forearm and left thigh lesion demonstrated a deep fungal infection and dense suppurative and granulomatous inflammation in the dermis centered around a follicle (Figure 2(a)), with budding yeast and hyphal forms within the follicle (Figure 2(b)), which was consistent with Majocchi's granuloma. PAS stain noted budding yeast forms, and Gram, AFB, and Fite stains were unrevealing. A deep fungal culture grew a very light growth of Malbranchea species, identified by morphology, with no evidence of histoplasmosis or blastomycosis. The patient was evaluated for immunosuppressive conditions and tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. Complete blood count and metabolic panel were normal.
The patient was prescribed itraconazole but could not obtain it secondary to financial reasons. Therefore, he was started on oral terbinafine for Majocchi's granuloma, and lesions started to resolve. Subsequent fungal blood cultures were negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old male presented with a 3-week history of worsening non-pruritic purple-to-dark-red papules and plaques spreading from his right knee to his left knee and bilateral upper extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Beginning in July 2016, the patient developed new non-pruritic circular purple/dark-red plaques and papules with minimal pustular drainage that differed from his baseline eczema, starting on the right knee and spreading to the left knee, bilateral extensor thighs, and circumferential upper extremities. A 3-week course of topical triamcinolone cream for presumed guttate psoriasis produced no improvement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Non-insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 6.5%), schizoaffective disorder, and eczema. Travel/social history: Traveled to Montana (April 2016) and New Mexico (2015) without acute illness; lived with his partner, had no pets, and denied sick contacts, international travel, or insect bites.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for spreading non-pruritic violaceous papules and plaques with minimal pustular drainage. Recent medication: topical triamcinolone cream.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous exam: purple-to-dark-red plaques and papules arranged in a discrete circular pattern without underlying erythema and with minimal pustular drainage over the full circumference of the bilateral upper extremities and bilateral extensor thighs, with relative sparing of sun-exposed skin.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel normal; HbA1c 6.5%; HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C serologies negative; fungal blood cultures negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Punch biopsies of left medial forearm and left thigh lesions: deep dermal perifollicular suppurative and granulomatous inflammation with budding yeast and hyphal forms within the hair follicle on H&E and PAS stains (Gram, AFB, and Fite stains negative). Deep tissue fungal culture: light growth of Malbranchea species identified by morphology, with no evidence of Histoplasma or Blastomyces.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Majocchi's granuloma caused by Malbranchea species (histoplasmosis and blastomycosis excluded by deep tissue fungal culture). Confirmation: Punch biopsy histopathology and PAS staining showing intrafollicular yeast and hyphal forms with perifollicular suppurative/granulomatous inflammation, and deep fungal culture isolating Malbranchea species. Plan & clinical course: Prescribed oral itraconazole initially, then switched to oral terbinafine due to financial constraints, resulting in resolution of the cutaneous lesions.
